answer: Each identity must commit a sealed plot, its storage kernel, before earning anything. Every epoch the chain demands proofs of those sectors; a plot referenced twice is flagged and its collateral slashed, so cloning storage pays nothing. A new key starts with no proved history, earning only a whisper of credit yet paying disk, sealing time and locked bond. The yarrow beacon reseeds proofs each round, so forking one history across many keys costs a full re-seal. Minting a thousand identities needs a thousand plots plus lost stake, pushing attack cost above reward.
